newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly down on Wednesday on overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,900 yuan ($2,880) per tonne, losing 90 yuan. It opened at 23,900 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,830 and a high of 23,920.
April fell 60 to 23,500, May 80 to 23,650, July 120 to 23,900, August 200 to 23,800 and September 100 to 23,750.
Combined volume fell to 52,040 tonnes from 69,940.
The contracts opened lower on Wednesday and moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
Market sentiment was steady but cautious due to the overnight LME losses, they said.
"The LME falls were the key factor in driving prices down today," one trader said.

"But a lot of speculators were seen building long positons at low levels as well," he added. "Many investors are still optimistic about the mid-term market trend, believing the current technical correction was reasonable."
Traders said copper was likely to move around current levels in the next few days on a lack of market-moving news.
"There is no stimulus in sight to push prices down or up sharply in the short term," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down across the board. April fell 50 to 16,300, May 30 to 16,700 and June 100 to 16,950.
Combined volume fell to 920 tonnes from 1,760.
